refused: apparmor: AppArmor restricts unprivileged user namespaces here, no rootlesskit profile is loaded, and this host's apparmor package ships none (Ubuntu's ships /etc/apparmor.d/rootlesskit from 24.04). Rootless Docker needs user namespaces, so admitting here means lifting the restriction for the whole host: every user and program on this host may then create unprivileged user namespaces again, the kernel attack surface the restriction exists to reduce. If it was turned on on purpose, keep it, and admit on another host instead. To lift it, run sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0; keep it at boot by writing kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 0 in /etc/sysctl.d/99-zz-paisans-userns.conf, which sorts after the files that set it, and changing every other line grep -rs apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns /etc/sysctl.conf /etc/sysctl.d /run/sysctl.d /usr/lib/sysctl.d finds; check sysctl kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns prints 0 after the next reboot; and admit again. Nothing was changed
